facts.text: The appellant landlord filed an application under Delhi Rent Control Act section 14(1)(b) seeking ejectment of the respondents.
facts.speaker: COURT
unknown: whether the application satisfied every prescribed procedural requirement

facts.text: The supplied opinion reports that all three lower courts concurrently found Gulzar Singh to be the sole tenant.
facts.speaker: COURT
facts.stage: Rent Controller, Tribunal and High Court findings
facts.quote: All the three courts concurrently found that Gulzar Singh was the sole tenant.

facts.text: The Rent Controller found that Gulzar Singh sublet the demised premises to Avtar Singh and ordered ejectment.
facts.speaker: COURT
unknown: target court acceptance of this finding
facts.quote: The Rent Controller and the Tribunal found that he sublet the demised premises to Avtar Singh, his brother and therefore ordered ejectment.

facts.text: The Rent Control Tribunal found that Gulzar Singh sublet the demised premises to Avtar Singh and ordered ejectment.
facts.speaker: COURT
unknown: target court acceptance of this finding
facts.quote: The Rent Controller and the Tribunal found that he sublet the demised premises to Avtar Singh, his brother and therefore ordered ejectment.

facts.text: The High Court found that Gulzar Singh did not sublet the premises to Avtar Singh and dismissed the ejectment petition on that premise.
facts.speaker: COURT
unknown: target court acceptance of this finding
facts.quote: and that he did not sublet the premises to Avtar Singh. On that premise the petition for ejectment was dismissed.

facts.text: The appellant landlord argued that the High Court committed gross error by interfering with the concurrent Rent Controller and Tribunal finding that Gulzar Singh had sublet the premises to Avtar Singh.
facts.speaker: LANDLORD
unknown: target court acceptance of the argument
facts.quote: the High Court has committed a gross error in interfering with the concurrent finding of fact

facts.text: Avtar Singh was reported to have claimed in an affidavit before the Income-Tax Authorities that he had exclusive possession as a tenant.
facts.speaker: THIRD_PARTY
unknown: full contents and context of the affidavit
facts.quote: in an affidavit filed by Avtar singh before Income-Tax Authorities he claimed exclusive possession as a tenant

facts.text: The appellant landlord argued, relying on section 18 of the Evidence Act, that Avtar Singh's asserted admission would bind Gulzar Singh.
facts.speaker: LANDLORD
unknown: whether the admission is legally binding on Gulzar Singh
target court acceptance of the evidentiary argument
facts.quote: the admission made by him would be binding on Gulzar Singh.

facts.text: The Rent Controller and Rent Control Tribunal relied on Avtar Singh's admission and other oral evidence and concluded that Avtar Singh alone was in exclusive possession and that subletting was proved.
facts.speaker: COURT
facts.stage: Rent Controller and Rent Control Tribunal evidentiary findings
unknown: target court acceptance of these lower-court findings
contents and weight of the unspecified other oral evidence
facts.quote: Avtar Singh alone was in exclusive possession and that, therefore, subletting was proved as a fact.

objects.text: premises bearing No. W.Z. 258/4, Subash Bazar, Nangal 540 Raya, New Jail Road, New Delhi
Avtar Singh affidavit before Income-Tax Authorities

relations.text: Avtar Singh is identified as the brother of Gulzar Singh.
relations.speaker: COURT

relations.text: The High Court found Gulzar Singh to be in exclusive possession of the premises.
relations.speaker: COURT
unknown: target court acceptance of this finding
relations.quote: the tenant was in exclusive possession of the premises bearing No. W.Z.

relations.text: The Rent Controller and Rent Control Tribunal found Avtar Singh alone to be in exclusive possession of the premises.
relations.speaker: COURT
relations.stage: Rent Controller and Rent Control Tribunal merits findings
unknown: target court acceptance of these findings
relations.quote: Avtar Singh alone was in exclusive possession

issue_needs_context_not_application_targ.text: Whether Gulzar Singh is the tenant whose conduct can engage the supplied Delhi Rent Control Act section 14(1)(b) ground.
Whether Gulzar Singh sublet, assigned, or otherwise parted with possession of all or part of the premises to Avtar Singh, preserving the conflicting lower-court findings.
Whether any relevant subletting, assignment, or parting with possession occurred with or without the landlord's written consent.
Whether any relevant transfer or subletting occurred within the statutory date scope, including on or after 9 June 1952 and, where applicable, after commencement of the Act.
Whether the supplied record establishes any notice, lawful-subletting, or protected-subtenant facts needed for the supplied sections 17 and 18 mechanisms.
